newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran urges understanding with Saudis before haj.
newsitem.headline: Iran urges understanding with Saudis before haj.

text.p: Iranian and Saudi leaders should iron out differences before the Moslem haj pilgrimage to ensure that the event is not marred by tensions between the two Gulf powers, an Iranian newspaper said on Tuesday.

"Rationalism demands that officials in both countries sit down together and sort out all relevant issues related to the haj affairs every year on the eve of the major religious duty," the English-language Iran News said in an editorial.
The newspaper often reflects the views of the Iranian foreign ministry.
"Pre-haj exchange of views by the two countries is a must to exterminate tension between the two major Islamic nations of the world."

The comments came one day after Iran vowed that its pilgrims would defy a Saudi ban and hold a political rally denouncing the United States and Israel at the mid-April haj, a pilgrimage to the holy city Mecca which draws up to two million Moslems from across the world to Saudi Arabia every year.
Radical Shi'ite Iran says its pilgrims should hold a rally denouncing the enemies of Islam as part of the annual haj.
Saudi Arabia's conservative Sunni rulers insist haj is a purely religious affair and should not be politicised. Riyadh has banned all political activities during haj in past years.
Saudi security forces clashed in 1987 with demonstrators in an Iranian-led rally in the streets of Mecca, killing about 400 people, mainly Iranians.

Iran boycotted the haj for the next three years. There has been no repeat of the bloodshed since the return of Iranian pilgrims in 1991 and their haj rallies have been low-key affairs often confined to the Iranian compounds.
Saudi Arabia has repeatedly warned pilgrims they would face tough punishment if they carried political material to haj, one of the five pillars of Islam.
